objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

## The one measured gap this round must close: the third token

Eight arms have been measured with the same width-20 beam forensics (57,439 rows).
Recall@10 is ordered by coverage, and coverage is the joint survival of the four positions:

| arm | recall@10 | coverage | alive L1/L2/L3/L4 | acc@1 T1/T2/T3/T4 | distinct T1/T2/T3/T4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| resample | **0.06363** | 0.0884 | .497/.122/.091/.088 | .098/.152/**.794**/**.977** | 241/256/256/**10** |
| l1_only | 0.06233 | 0.0855 | 1.000/.829/.156/.086 | 1.000/.175/.106/.557 | 1/94/256/37 |
| l1_br_euclid | 0.06207 | 0.0847 | 1.000/.829/.161/.085 | 1.000/.178/.115/.550 | 1/80/256/44 |
| successor_geodesic_coarse (v1) | 0.05486 | 0.0740 | .989/.341/.122/.074 | .248/.180/**.338**/.737 | 26/223/256/68 |
| successor_geodesic_coarse (v2, curved behaviour-ordered extension) | 0.05529 | - | - | - | 28/... |
| tangent_successor_residual | 0.05500 | 0.0731 | .643/.180/.090/.073 | .121/.187/**.527**/**.885** | 238/251/256/**27** |
| successor_entropy | 0.05122 | 0.0688 | .735/.400/.133/.069 | .262/.338/.412/.680 | 250/211/256/91 |
| l1_br | 0.04671 | 0.0678 | 1.000/1.000/1.000/.068 | 1.000/1.000/1.000/.008 | 1/1/1/16462 |

Three findings are now solid:

1. **A coarse first level is nearly free** (v1: 26 codes, gold first token alive 98.9%,
   T1 accuracy 0.248), and it is *not* what holds recall back.
2. **Ordering the extension token by a behaviour-informed curved rank changes almost
   nothing** (v2: 0.05529 against v1's 0.05486), because the tail was already the cheapest
   part of these arms.
3. **The third position is the discriminator that separates the best arm from every other
   arm**: `resample` is correct 79.4% of the time at T3 (and 97.7% at T4 over ten extension
   values), while every other arm is between 0.106 and 0.527 at T3. Its first level is the
   *worst* (0.497) and it still wins, because once the path survives to T2 the rest is
   nearly determined.

## What must be designed

A mechanism that makes the **third code nearly determined by the first two codes and the
train-only behaviour structure** — i.e. a residual-level behavioural clustering, not a
first-level one. Concretely the proposal must target T3 top-1 well above 0.53 (towards
0.7-0.8) while keeping the first level cheap and the fourth token a small near-deterministic
extension, and must keep a genuine behaviour-conditioned hyperbolic computation on one
connected path (the curvature and the geodesic distance must change which codes the
residual quantizer chooses at levels 2 and 3).

The behaviour signal is the train-only directed successor structure (counts, smoothed
distributions, or a learned successor prototype) computed from training histories only. The
mechanism may use it as a contrastive/triplet term on the *residual* codes, as a curved
assignment cost at levels 2-3, or as a curved consensus among successor codes — but it must
be one connected computation whose removal changes the emitted SID.

Out of scope: renumbering the first level only; a pure capacity change; a penalty on the
fourth token; a second disconnected loss whose gradient never reaches the assignment.

## Required measurement contract

State, for the mechanism: the predicted direction of `L1 Hard ER` (canonical 52,855 pairs
with ten fixed negatives), gold-prefix survival at depths 1-4, the teacher-forced top-1
accuracy of T3 and T4, and Stage 3 `test_R@10` (target > 0.065). Define the three arms
(both-on, behaviour-off, geometry-off) and state where the curve acts at each level.

## Frozen constraints

Four-token fixed-width SID with the deterministic collision-extension token, 3000 Stage 2
epochs on four cards, no early stopping, no test-time tuning, the frozen Stage 3 protocol,
no validation or test behaviour in SID construction. Keep the cost near the baseline: a
candidate whose one-epoch smoke is far slower than the baseline's (0.13 s/epoch) is
rejected.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
